The cause is a sign bug in [truth.py](file:///work/clinicbench/truth.py#L130-L134) inside `_booking`:

```python
    if basis == "self_pay":
        cost = W.SELF_PAY[spec]
        t["payment"].update(claim="dont_submit", selfpay_willing="yes",
                            selfpay_max=cost - rng.choice([0, 50, 100, 200]),
                            conditional_on_coverage=rng.random() < 0.5)
```

Because `selfpay_max` subtracts `rng.choice([0, 50, 100, 200])` instead of adding it, 75% of `selfpay_booking` patients are generated with `selfpay_max < cost`. Once the clinician states the price, `PatientPolicy.respond` in [policy.py](file:///work/clinicbench/policy.py#L410-L427) sees `selfpay_max < cost`, flips `selfpay_willing` to `"no"`, and `PatientPolicy._in_truth` in [policy.py](file:///work/clinicbench/policy.py#L314-L316) refuses the booking offer. (By contrast, `selfpay_retraction` in [truth.py](file:///work/clinicbench/truth.py#L232-L239) explicitly overrides `selfpay_max` to `cost - rng.choice([50, 100])` after calling `_booking`.)

Since [truth.py](file:///work/clinicbench/truth.py) is frozen instrument code listed in [phase3-freeze.json](file:///work/docs/phase3-freeze.json#L8), this is a `fix`.

```json
{"kind": "fix", "files": ["clinicbench/truth.py"], "symbols": ["clinicbench.truth._booking"], "cause": "In clinicbench.truth._booking, selfpay_max is set to cost - rng.choice([0, 50, 100, 200]) instead of adding the offset, so 75% of selfpay_booking patients have a maximum below the visit cost and retract self-pay willingness as soon as the price is stated.", "attribution": null}
```

Fixed `selfpay_max` in `_booking` in [truth.py](file:///work/clinicbench/truth.py#L130-L134) by adding the random offset instead of subtracting it (`cost + rng.choice([0, 50, 100, 200])`).

### Verification
- Verified with `python3` that `clinicbench.truth.build("selfpay_booking", ...)` produces `selfpay_max >= cost` for 20/20 sampled seeds, while `selfpay_retraction` still produces `selfpay_max < cost` for 20/20 sampled seeds.
- Note: `pytest` is not installed in the container environment, so the `tests/` suite could not be executed.
